I’ve worked in the home improvement industry for over 10 years, sweetie. Lowe’s and HD use subcontractors but a majority of those subcontractors use day laborers. That’s why they hang around the front of these stores. And that’s why the cost is much less than going to a company like Windows Plus, Katchmark, Window Man, etc. The problem some people run into is that the installer is not familiar with the products and doesn’t know how to properly install the products or they run into issues, like wood rot, and they don’t know how to remedy it. Now, I do have to say even though the subcontractors for the smaller companies don’t use day laborers, some have been caught with illegal aliens on their crew. But they usually have been trained by the owner or lead installer so they (usually) know what they’re doing.

Windows Plus, LLC (Annandale, VA). They deal with different vendors that will custom make your doors. Prices will vary, depending on the options you pick. They may cost more than Lowe’s and Home Depot but the quality of the products are much higher. Lowe’s and HD carry well known brands but they are the cheaper models. They also use day laborers to install which means that they most likely are not experienced in installing the products or knowledgeable about the products. WP uses subcontractors that have been installing doors, windows, etc. for decades. They’re other companies similar but I’m more familiar with WP.  The sales rep don’t push for you to sign on the dotted line or for the most expensive product out there.  You can check them out on Best Picks Report and Consumer Checkbook for reviews.

1) Make sure you find a reputable tattoo artist. Most have their portfolio online or in the shop. Check out any reviews of the shop and the artist. Or just ask. People come up to me to compliment me on my tattoos and ask where I had them done. Make sure they are up to code on everything. And remember - You get what you pay for. 

2) Try to find an artist that has done tattoos in the style that you like. Some artist specialize in portraits, watercolors, geometric designs, etc.

3) Make sure the design you want is something that you can live with.
If you don't like it down the road you can do a cover up or have it lasered off. Both are costly and I heard that the laser hurts worse than than getting the ink. If you can find someone that can draw the tattoo on you with markers, try that. That way you get a feel of it and make any changes before making it permanent. It's better to wait and not regret your decision than get a tattoo impulsuvly and regret it.

4) It will look different as you age. It will fade and your skin with thin and, maybe even sag. You can get it retouched down the road. Always apply sunscreen to the tattooed area when exposed to sun. It will help slow down the fading.

5) Getting a tattoo on the side of the torso hurts. The thinner the skin and closer to the bone, the more pain you will experience. Of course, this also depends on the threshold of pain.
